title: connection sync holdoff and surge insulation to protect SLOs during regional warmups
author: Elena Park
release_notes: Adds a holdoff gate for connection sync to prevent synchronized KV/egress bursts during regional warmups; introduces a surge-insulation policy that smooths tenant-level egress and favors gradual backoff before hard shedding. Includes telemetry and a hotfix for a circuit-state race observed in production.
description:
Motivation: During the 2025-10-30 regional incident we observed large cohorts of connections performing KV-sync + prefix rehydrate at near-identical times when new nodes came online or during controlled rollouts. The synchronized work created short egress spikes that tripped tenant SLO enforcement and caused downstream circuit hysteresis. This PR introduces two orthogonal mitigations: (1) a connection sync holdoff that staggers KV/rehydration work based on an epochal jitter + server-load probe, and (2) a surge-insulation policy that places a short smoothing buffer on tenant egress accounting so the SLO enforcer prefers transient slowdowns and probing over immediate hard shedding. This is implemented as a conservative default that can be tuned per-deployment.

What changed (summary):
- runtime: add connection_sync_holdoff (epochal jitter + load-aware delay) to the serving runtime connection manager; this delays synchronous KV rehydrates and batches them into micro-waves to avoid spike amplification.
- slo: new surge_insulator policy that applies an exponential smoothing window to tenant egress rate before it contributes to short-window SLO violation counters; configurable via defaults and per-tenant overrides.
- fix: address race in circuit state transitions when manual unpark and automatic reopen occur concurrently; introduce a lightweight state mutex and ordering invariant.
- telemetry: new metrics (conn_sync.delay_ms, surge_insulator.smoothed_egress, surge_insulator.drop_reason) and a new debug view for correlated connection sync spikes.
- ops: helm values and defaults.toml knobs to opt-in/out and tune windows for Dedicated/Private installs.

- [x] Design doc reviewed with SRE and Runtime (ENG-2872)
- [x] Unit tests for connection_holdoff jitter and ordering
- [x] Integration test exercising warmup-inserted micro-waves
- [x] Canary deployment in us-west-2 for 24h
- [x] Telemetry dashboards and alerts added

Commits:
- "add: connection_sync_holdoff gate + epochal jitter (runtime)"
- "feat: surge_insulator smoothing policy and config plumbing (slo subsystem)"
- "fix: circuit state raceguard and tests"
- "docs: add operational knobs and example helm values"

Changed files (high level):
- src/runtime/connection_manager.rs (new holdoff logic, unit tests)
- src/slo/surge_insulator.go (policy implementation + config hooks)
- services/slo/enforcer.rs (integration with smoothed metrics)
- telemetry/telemetry_schema.yaml (new metrics)
- deploy/helm/values.yaml (tunable knobs + docs)
- config/defaults.toml (insulation defaults for hosted/dedicated)
- tests/ci/connection_sync_test.py (new integration test harness)

Testing and CI:
- Local unit-tests: all green
- Integration: connection_sync_test added and run in CI, initially flaky under race conditions; fixed by adding a deterministic wait in harness and re-running.
- CI checks: lint, unit, integration, e2e-canary. First run: integration flake (timeout); rerun passed. Final CI: all checks green.

Review notes / conversation (highlights):
- Marco Liu (reviewer): "Nice approach separating smoothing from enforcement. Please add a high-cardinality knob off switch for hot paths and ensure the egress smoothing metric tags tenant and route." — addressed in surge_insulator.go and telemetry_schema.yaml in commit 2.
- Sofia Patel: "Can you quantify added latency for connection warmups under holdoff? We should ensure 95p isn't increased materially." — author reply: "Added micro-benchmarks in connection_manager.rs; median increase is ~4ms for first token rehydrate, 95p < 15ms under our simulated warmup. Bench numbers included in PR description and surfaced to telemetry as conn_sync.delay_ms." — Sofia approved after bench numbers were attached.
- Dinesh Ramesh: "Concern: SLO enforcer might hide persistent noisiness if window is too wide. Suggest a decay-based fallback into hard-shed for sustained violations." — author: "Surge_insulator is exponential-smoothing with configurable half-life; added a fallback threshold that short-circuits to the enforcer if smoothed_rate > sustained_threshold for duration X. Config keys documented in defaults.toml." — resolved.
- QA (automated): flagged integration flake; root-caused to harness timing; fixed and re-run.

Operational plan and rollout:
- Step 1 (canary): deploy to us-west-2 with surge-insulator enabled for system tenants only (24h), monitor conn_sync.delay_ms and smoothed_egress.
- Step 2 (staggered): after canary, enable for 10% of production Dedicated clusters and observe telemetry for 72h.
- Step 3: full rollout with per-tenant opt-out until baseline observed.

Why this is different from prior mitigations: Existing shedding logic reacts quickly to short-window surges which is correct for malicious or sustained overloads but amplifies synchronized benign work (rehydrates/warmups). This change intentionally creates a temporary inertia to absorb microbursts while preserving the enforcer's ability to escalate for persistent issues. That reduces false-positive SLO violations and avoids cascading circuit flips.

Follow-ups (future work):
- Explore collaborative tenant warmup scheduling from control-plane (coordinated warming) for major rollouts.
- Add adaptive holdoff that uses predictive load curves instead of fixed jitter in high-variance regions.
